scope: Close a real-browser verification gap for the already-draggable canvas toolbar: drag the canvas region before or after a dock and prove the local workspace layout remains undoable, reloadable, and canvas-safe without invoking page Save or Publish.

gap_and_result.verified_gap: The existing production UI marks .canvas-toolbar draggable and the drop handler supports sourceId=canvas, but the native mouse suite only exercised left/right dock sources. A real native mouse test was absent for the canvas source path.
gap_and_result.initial_probe: The first targeted run's expected order for inserting the canvas before the right dock from canvas-left-right was incorrect; the actual left-canvas-right result matches the documented insertion rule. Correcting that test expectation revealed no runtime defect.
gap_and_result.result: No runtime change was warranted. The test now drives the browser's native mouse/HTML drag lifecycle from the plain-text right edge of the actual canvas toolbar, covers six starting orders and both insertion directions, checks undo/redo and reload, and protects the no-page-write boundary.

coverage.browser: Real Chromium using the existing Playwright local editor fixture; native mouse Locator.dragTo, not synthetic DragEvent dispatch.
assertions: canvas toolbar can be the native drag source
drop zone cue and drag state clear after each operation
workspace status describes the canvas and target dock in plain language
canvas retains a dedicated visible grid track of at least 400 CSS px
the selected order is saved only to the allowlisted workspace preference
Undo/Redo restores/reapplies the final canvas move
the final order survives a complete Editor reload
the fixture records zero Page Model Save, Publish, or renderer requests
left and right dock rectangles do not overlap the canvas grid region
desktop layout has no horizontal document overflow at 1280 CSS px
